captures.q: U.S. Copyright Office Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
captures.description: THE INITIATIVE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The U.S. Copyright Office (USCO) maintains that U.S. law strictly requires human authorship for copyright protection, and has released a multi-part analysis addressing digital replicas, generative AI outputs, and AI model training.' Core policy and reports (the launch and 'a Notice of Inquiry on August 20, 2023'; Parts 1 to 3 with dates); key legal precedents (Thaler v. Perlmutter; the disclosure rule); an offer of registration decisions 'such as Zarya of the Dawn'. Seven cards: three Copyright Office pages, Skadden, Crowell & Moring, WIPO, Congress.gov.

atoms.evidence: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence | U.S. Copyright Office
The U.S. Copyright Office (USCO) maintains that U.S. law strictly requires human authorship for copyright protection
The USCO launched its comprehensive AI initiative in early 2023
has released a multi-part analysis addressing digital replicas, generative AI outputs, and AI model training.
Part 2: Copyrightability of Generative AI Outputs (Published January 29, 2025)
Applicants must disclose any more-than-de minimis AI-generated material when submitting a work for registration and describe the specific human contribution.
